title: Level 1 project: a tip and split calculator
lesson:
Put HTML, CSS and JavaScript together into a small app people actually use: a **bill splitter** for a group eating out or sharing costs. Two files: 1. **ex1_split.html**: a page with labelled inputs `bill` (number), `tip` (a select with 0, 5, 10 and 15 percent), `people` (number, min 1), and an output `

`. Style it so it's comfortable on a phone (viewport, max-width, inputs full width, a big readable result). Link `ex2_split.js` at the end of the body. 2. **ex2_split.js**: a pure function `split(bill, tipPercent, people)` returning the amount each person pays, as a number rounded UP to the nearest whole shilling (nobody wants to be 0.33 short), or `null` if the inputs make no sense (empty, negative, zero people). Then wire it: whenever any input changes, show `Each pays 1,234 KSh` (use `toLocaleString()` for the comma) or `Fill in the bill and people` if `split` gives null. Plan first: the HTML ids, then the function (test it in your head with 1000 KSh, 10%, 3 people: 1100 / 3 = 366.67, so 367), then the wiring.

notes: Math.ceil rounds up; toLocaleString adds thousands separators.

exercises.title: The page
exercises.prompt: Build the page as the lesson describes: inputs bill, tip (select), people, output each, labels for all, the viewport tag, some CSS (at least a max-width), and the script link to ex2_split.js.
exercises.starter: Split the bill

tests.name: no errors (and the script file is found)

exercises.solution:
Split the bill

Fill in the bill and people

exercises.title: The calculator
exercises.prompt: Write split(bill, tipPercent, people) and the wiring, as the lesson describes.

tests.check: const b = document.getElementById("bill"), t = document.getElementById("tip"), p = document.getElementById("people"); b.value = "1000"; t.value = "10"; p.value = "3"; for (const el of [b, t, p]) { el.dispatch("input"); el.dispatch("change"); } const txt = document.getElementById("each").textContent; if (!/367/.test(txt)) throw new Error("with 1000, 10% and 3 people the page should show 367; it shows: " + txt);
tests.name: the page updates

hints: Convert all three with Number(); return null if any is not finite, bill < 0, tip < 0 or people < 1 (and treat "" as missing).
Wire it: one function update() that reads the three values and sets each.textContent; add it as the "input" and "change" listener on all three.

quiz.q: Why keep split() separate from the DOM code?
choices: A pure function can be tested on its own and reused anywhere

quiz.q: Why Math.ceil for each person's share?
choices: So the total collected is never short

quiz.q: Why listen to both input and change?
choices: Typing fires input; choosing in a select fires change

cards.a: Pure functions for the logic; thin DOM code for display.

explain: Explain level 1 project: a tip and split calculator to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
